Refinery.name: Volatiles Refinery
Refinery.description:
There is a living in that rock. Fennmark's V4 helps you get at it before a buyer tells you what it is worth. Water from hydrates, metal stock from meteoric iron, carbon from carbon ore: a working hold can become more than a place to stack tomorrow's sale. The {2} x {2} plant weighs {0:F0} kg and draws {1:F0} kW on shift.

The V4 also handles clay hydrates, ammonium salt crust and Lixivar leached residue. Its range includes nickel steel, methane cracking, carbon and straw processing, and another working life for spent CO2 scrubber cartridges and EVA filters. Solids collect in the tray; water and recovered gas need linked silos and stores, touching the plant or joined by the appropriate line.

Leave room in the budget for cooling and scrubbing. Carbon ore and salt crust release gas into the cabin, and a melt left waiting too long for a cool room becomes slag. Fennmark sells the plant. Keeping a working ship around it is still a captain's trade.

Material.PhobosNickelIronIngot_descripti: A 4 kg ingot cast from meteoric iron as it comes: iron with a few percent of nickel and a trace of cobalt. Sound structural stock for machining, and the feed for nickel steel. Not steel by itself.
Material.PhobosNickelSteelIngot_descript: A 4 kg ingot of nickel steel, carburised in the refinery from four nickel-iron ingots and a kilogram of carbon. Tougher than plain steel and worth more: the best thing a lump of meteoric iron can become aboard.
Material.PhobosCarbonBlack_description: A kilogram of fine soot-black carbon, cracked out of methane in the refinery. Burn it there with stored oxygen for carbon dioxide your crops can use, or sell it; it is worth little.
Material.PhobosExhaustedSorbent_descript: The scrubber cartridge that could not be saved: one in four is lost when the refinery restores used cartridges. Its shell and spent gas-absorbing material cannot be recovered.
Material.PhobosPlantAsh_description: The pinch of mineral ash a straw bale leaves when the refinery burns or chars it. Nothing more comes out of it; carry it out of the tray and sell or discard it.
Material.PhobosSpentMash_description: What is left in the vats after a fermenter-still charge: pulp, yeast and sugar that did not ferment. Nothing more comes out of it; carry it out of the tray and sell or discard it.
Material.PhobosAlembrineSpirit_descripti: A 35 g measure of clear spirit at 40% alcohol, bottled aboard from your own beets. It drinks like any other liquor: a lift for morale, a hazard for judgement. Not for the reactor.
Material.PhobosCarbonStock_description: One kilogram of carbon driven out of carbon ore in the refinery. Melted in excess with four nickel-iron ingots it makes nickel steel; alone, with a methane store linked, it is the bed that cracks methane into carbon black and hydrogen.
Material.PhobosRefinerySlag_description: A kilogram of dirty leftovers skimmed from a metal melt, or a frozen batch broken out of the hearth. Nothing more can be recovered from it.
Material.PhobosAnhydrousResidue_descript: Eight kilograms of baked clay with its water driven off. Nothing more can be recovered from it.
Material.PhobosClayHydrates_description: A chunk of dark, water-rich clay minerals of the kind sampled from carbonaceous asteroids, about a fifth of it bound water. Bake it in a refinery for water; the government kiosks buy it like other ore.

Sabatier.name: Sabatier Reactor
Sabatier.description:
Your crew has already paid for that breath. Fennmark's K2 gets some water back from the CO2 left behind, and makes methane for the next job. A two-by-two reactor weighing {0:F0} kg, built for captains who would rather carry a little chemistry than buy everything twice.

A one-hour CO2 cycle draws {1:F1} kW, taking {2:F3} kg of hydrogen from a linked store and {3:F3} kg of CO2 from an installed canister within one tile. The return is {4:F3} kg of water and {5:F3} kg of methane, each to its own linked vessel. With an X2, this route recovers about half the water used to make the hydrogen. Some still leaves with the methane; plan your replenishment accordingly.

The K2 also accepts a carbon monoxide store as its carbon source, returning methane and water from an Oxsmith CR-4's gas. An X2 can then separate the water for oxygen. Every partner needs its own power, and the K2's reaction warms the room. A useful return on yesterday's supplies, without a promise of endless supplies.

Manifold.name: RCS Propellant Manifold
Manifold.description:
A hold full of propellant should do more than look reassuring. Fennmark's P1 puts bulk gas stores behind your RCS, through a {0:F0} kg valve block that asks for no electricity. It fits a gas-input tile on the RCS Intake Regulator, where a canister would otherwise sit.

Choose the stores and whether they supply the thrusters before or after the regulator's own canisters. Touching stores or a gas line complete the connection. All feeds arrive switched off, ready for your selection. A kilogram of methane gives about 1.45 times nitrogen's push; hydrogen gives about 3.7 times. That is a reason to choose your propellant carefully, and to remember that the ship still has to stop.

Leach.name: Leach and Crystallise Unit
Leach.description:
Rock rarely arrives sorted into what your ship needs. Lixivar's LC-3 does the wet work: useful salts out of evaporite and olivine, fertiliser from recovered phosphate, hydrogen from ferrosilicon. A {2} x {2} unit, {0:F0} kg and {1:F0} kW while working, for a captain ready to sell something better than an unexamined chunk.

Its recipes cover potassium sulfate, phosphate concentrate, Epsom salt, struvite and ammonium sulfate. With Phobos Agriculture aboard, the LC-3 also prepares Groundwork makeup salts and complete crop nutrients. Select the recipe and supply its water, ammonia, hydrogen or acid vessels through touching equipment or the matching line; crop nutrients need a hopper within one tile. Solids collect in the tray, including the residue and salt cake the chemistry leaves behind. Allow for room heat and safe acid handling. There is value to recover here, and a little honest cleaning up afterwards.

Feeder.description:
Slingwright has a proposition for the slag taking up your hold: give it one last job on the way out. The RM-1 grinds supported cakes, rejects, tailings and other process remainders into reaction mass for the RCS. One tile, {0:F0} kg empty, with room for {1:F0} kg of prepared mass and a working draw of {2:F0} kW.

Fit it where an RCS gas canister would go. Its mass gives the same push per kilogram as nitrogen; it still takes real material to move a ship. Useful stock belongs elsewhere, and unsupported cargo stays cargo. The RM-1 is for the remainder of the job, when hauling it to the next buyer has ceased to look attractive.

Cell.name: Electrolysis Cell
Cell.description:
Oxsmith starts with a simple question: why pass good oxygen on the way to buying another canister? The EC-4 takes loose regolith or Silicates ore and separates oxygen from the molten rock. Ferrosilicon and slag collect in the tray; a regolith lump's trace water goes to a silo. Plant for captains whose next berth is a choice they would like to keep.

The {2} x {2} cell weighs {0:F0} kg and draws {1:F0} kW while working. A regolith lump yields 3.9 kg of oxygen in an hour; Silicates ore yields 2.6 kg in 40 minutes. Connect an oxygen store and water silo through touching equipment or their lines.

Provide air and cooling in the workroom. Regolith releases a little CO2, and a hot room holds up the cell. A waiting melt can freeze and be melted again without losing the charge. The oxygen is in the rock. Getting it out still costs power, time and upkeep.

Carbothermal.name: Carbothermal Reactor
Carbothermal.description:
Every berth has somebody willing to sell you air. Oxsmith would rather sell you the means to make your own. The CR-4 puts methane to work on loose regolith or Silicates ore, recovering the rock's oxygen as carbon monoxide, with hydrogen for the next process and ferrosilicon and slag in the tray.

The {2} x {2} reactor weighs {0:F0} kg and draws {1:F0} kW while working, half the EC-4's draw. Pair it with a Fennmark K2 and X2 to finish the oxygen route: the K2 turns carbon monoxide and hydrogen into methane and water, and the X2 separates that water. A regolith lump's 6.83 kg of carbon monoxide represents about 3.9 kg of oxygen, with methane recovered for another charge. Those partner machines have power bills of their own.

Connect methane, carbon monoxide and hydrogen stores, plus a water silo, by touching equipment or the appropriate lines. Allow for heat and a little CO2 from regolith. Carbon monoxide is poisonous: keep its storage sound. More choice about your next port starts with looking after the plant.
